text: Imagine you're a French soldier. It's August 1914, and you're marching to war in bright red trousers.
Across the fields, the Germans are wearing grey. You can barely see them.
They can see you just fine.
So why would an army dress its men like targets?
Go back a hundred years. Every musket shot made a cloud of thick white smoke.
After a few volleys, the whole battlefield vanished, and bright colours helped you tell friend from enemy.
Then a new gunpowder cleared the smoke, and those red trousers became a bullseye.
